what_the_eye_sees: A gear or sprocket ring: a flat gold washer with a row of square cog teeth on top and short radial slots punched round the side, like sun rays or a bike chainring. Face-on it becomes a toothed crown or sunburst with one small cross at the top. No pointed arch, no lancet niches, no leaf crockets, nothing that says Gothic cathedral. The section shows why: the body is a bell or bottle shape (wide rounded feet, curving shoulders) with a straight-sided rectangular fin standing up off the top, so the crest is a flat-topped wall and not a keel, and the arch never comes to a point.
changes: Section (feature 2 and the crest fin): remove the vertical rectangular fin that rises about 1.4 mm straight off the shoulders, and let the two flank arcs meet in a single sharp apex. Today the crest is a flat cap 1.5 mm wide on parallel walls. Each flank should run unbroken from springer to apex, so the profile is a true lancet. Acceptance: section.png shows one closed pointed-arch outline with no straight vertical segment above the springers, and the side view shows one bright ridge line on the crest, not a slab.

Crockets (feature 5 / pattern 9): replace the square tabs with curled leaf crockets that hook forward along theta, each at least 1.8 mm long and 1.2 mm proud of the keel, with a visible open curl (hook gap of at least 0.6 mm). Drop the count from 13 to 9–11 so each one reads as a separate leaf at 300 px. Acceptance: in hero-300 and face-300 no crocket shows a flat top or square corner, and each one has a crook a viewer can see as a leaf hook.

Niches (features 11–13): make them read as pointed lancet windows, not slots. Widen them from 0.9 to about 1.3 mm and lengthen them from 1.2 to about 2.2 mm, give each a sharp pointed head toward the crest with a flat sill toward the bore, sink them at least 0.8 mm, and cut the count to about 24 a side. Acceptance: in hero-300 each niche shows a visible pointed head and a shadowed floor, and a viewer counting them sees a row of tiny arched windows rather than ray slots.
